title: Sample Efficiency Playbook for Annotated Probe Budgets
author: Marisa Ortega
body:
Overview

This playbook defines a standard approach for maximizing sample efficiency when running annotated probes across production-like workloads. It prescribes budgeting, stratified sampling, annotation contracts, and active reuse techniques so evaluation teams get high-value signals under constrained annotation budgets. The procedures are intended for evaluation engineers, data stewards, and model owners who run continuous and episodic probe campaigns.

Goals and success metrics

- Primary goal: maximize signal-to-cost (meaningful failures detected per annotation dollar).
- Business KPIs we influence: regression detection velocity, annotation cost per unique failure type, mean-time-to-triage (MTTT).
- Operational metrics (recommended targets):
  - Probe precision target: >= 0.75 (fraction of flagged probes that require action).
  - Per-slice effective sample size (ESS): >= 200 for critical slices monthly.
  - Annotation spend adherence: actual spend within +/- 10% of monthly probe budget.

When to use this playbook

- Regular cadence evaluation (daily/weekly probes) where annotation budgets are limited.
- Ad-hoc investigations of suspected drift where labeling resources must be prioritized.
- Pre-rollout validation for quantized or cache-sensitive model variants with constrained annotation windows.

Roles and ownership

- Probe Owner: owns probe design, sampling config, and triage handoff. (Typically evaluation engineer).
- Annotation Steward: manages vendor contracts, annotation SLAs, and quality checks.
- Model Owner: consumes annotated signals and implements fixes or rollbacks.
- Budget Owner: finance or program lead who authorizes monthly annotation budgets.

Key concepts (short definitions)

- Annotated Probe: a probe executed against a workload that results in human annotation for correctness/quality.
- Budgeted Probe Campaign: probe execution plan constrained by a fixed annotation budget (dollars or human-hours).
- Stratum (slice): a workload segment defined by feature predicates (e.g., locale=en-AU, long_context>1024, intent=invoice-parsing).

High-level approach

1) Define the hypothesis and slices: start with 3–7 slices prioritized by business risk (customer impact), prior failure rate, and expected volume.
2) Allocate budget across slices using a stratified economy (baseline + adaptive top-up).
3) Use hybrid sampling (stratified + uncertainty-driven) in each stratum.
4) Apply reuse and augmentation: deduplicate candidates, reuse previous annotations where valid, and synthesize low-cost probes for low-risk slices.
5) Triage pipeline: automatically route high-severity flagged probes to rapid reviewer queues.

Budget allocation template (recommended default)

| Slice priority | Minimum pct budget | Adaptive top-up rule | Target ESS (monthly) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Critical (customer-facing errors) | 40% | If failure rate > 0.5% increase by +20% | 300 | Manual review SLA: 24h |
| High (frequent but low-severity) | 25% | Top-up if uncertainty > 0.2 | 250 | Use targeted synthetic augmentation |
| Medium (edge clusters) | 20% | Top-up if drift score > baseline | 200 | Prioritize diverse examples |
| Low (long tail) | 15% | No auto top-up; periodic refresh | 100 | Prefer automated heuristics/weak labels |

Sampling algorithm guidance

- Step 1: Stratified reservoir sampling per stratum to ensure minimum coverage.
- Step 2: Within each stratum, score candidates with an uncertainty score (model ensemble disagreement, entropy, or calibration gap).
- Step 3: Combine scores with recency and novelty rank: final_score = 0.6 * uncertainty + 0.3 * novelty + 0.1 * recency.
- Step 4: Run capped top-K selection per stratum respecting the allocated budget.

Example scoring pseudo-YAML (for scheduler config)

scheduler_config: |
  sampling_policy: "stratified_uncertainty"
  strata: ["critical", "high", "medium", "low"]
  stratum_min_coverage: {critical: 0.4, high: 0.25, medium: 0.2, low: 0.15}
  scoring_weights: {uncertainty: 0.6, novelty: 0.3, recency: 0.1}
  max_annotations_per_campaign: 2000
  reuse_window_days: 90

Annotation economy techniques (practical tactics)

- Pairwise adjudication: only for critical slices; otherwise single-pass annotation with gold-checks to reduce cost.
- Conditional adjudication: use consensus threshold (e.g., when annotator disagreement > 0.25) to trigger second pass.
- Hierarchical labels: collect coarse labels first (binary pass/fail) and only expand to fine-grained taxonomy when the coarse label is fail.
- Weak-label seeding: use heuristic or model-based weak labels to triage low-risk candidates and reserve human labels for ambiguous cases.
- Partial annotation: annotate just the token span or specific fields instead of full-text when that suffices for failure detection.

Quality controls and SLAs

- Annotation accuracy gate: sample 5% of annotations for gold review; accuracy must be >= 92% for campaign acceptance.
- Turnaround SLA: critical probes annotated within 24 hours; standard probes within 72 hours.
- Inter-annotator agreement (IAA): target Cohen's kappa >= 0.6 for binary pass/fail tasks.

Operational runbook (step-by-step)

1) Pre-campaign (72h before):
   - Confirm hypothesis, slices, and proposed budget with Model Owner and Budget Owner.
   - Check reuse window and exclude recently annotated examples (reuse_window_days).
   - Lock sampling policy in the scheduler_config.
2) Launch campaign:
   - Start probe collection and sample selection.
   - Push selected candidates to annotation platform with expected SLA.
3) During campaign (real-time):
   - Monitor annotation burn rate and ESS per slice. If spend > 70% of budget and ESS < target, apply adaptive downsampling on low-priority slices.
   - Auto-route high-severity failures to expedited triage (Slack channel and Pager duty).
4) Post-campaign (24–72h after):
   - Run acceptance checks (accuracy gate, IAA).
   - Publish annotated dataset metadata and pass to Model Owner.
   - If campaign identified actionable regression, open triage ticket with required rollback/fix recommendations.

Decision rules and escalation

- If annotation accuracy < 92%: pause campaign and do a 100-sample gold calibration; annotation steward must resolve before resuming.
- If untriaged high-severity failure count > 10 for a critical slice: escalate to Model Owner and SRE on-call.
- If spend > 110% of budget: automatically freeze non-critical active campaigns and notify Budget Owner.

Annotation data model and metadata (minimum fields)

- probe_id (string)
- stratum (string)
- sample_ts (ISO8601)
- model_version (string)
- input_features (JSON blob, allowed as string)
- coarse_label (pass|fail)
- fine_label (taxonomy code or empty)
- annotator_id (string)
- annotation_ts (ISO8601)
- review_flags (list of short codes)
- provenance_tags (list of short tags)

Example CLI to start a budgeted campaign

# start a 1,500-label campaign using sampling policy config file
redwood-eval-cli campaign start --name "invoice-priming-q1" --policy-file ./configs/invoice-budget-policy.yaml --labels 1500 --priority critical,high --owner marisa.ortega@redwood.com

Cost modeling quick reference (unit numbers are illustrative)

- Average single-pass annotation cost: $0.90 per sample
- Adjudication pass: additional $0.45 per sample when used
- Gold-check overhead: 5% of labels reviewed manually (cost absorbed in vendor contract)
- Monthly budget example: $12,000 -> ~13,333 single-pass labels -> allocate per table above

Common anti-patterns (and what to do instead)

- Anti-pattern: uniformly sampling across everything.
  - Remedy: stratify and prioritize by business impact and prior failure density.
- Anti-pattern: annotation-first without reuse.
  - Remedy: always deduplicate and check reuse window before assigning tags to annotators.
- Anti-pattern: chasing low-variance slices with tiny budgets.
  - Remedy: group low-volume strata and use weak-label seeding.

Appendix: useful queries and dashboards

- "Probe Budget Dashboard" must show per-campaign spend, ESS per slice, per-slice failure rate, top failure types, and time-to-triage percentiles.
- Useful SQL snippet (pseudocode) to compute ESS per slice:
  SELECT stratum, effective_sample_size(count, variance_estimate) FROM probe_annotations WHERE campaign_id = 'X' GROUP BY stratum;
